    """Bring ``suite`` in line with a document: create the checks it lacks, update the
    ones that differ, and with ``prune`` delete the ones the document does not name.
    Checks are matched by NAME. ``dry_run`` returns the plan without writing — that plan
    is the drift between the document and the workspace.

    The whole document is validated first, so a refused document changes nothing. Each
    change then goes through the same service call a UI edit uses, so it gets its own
    version and audit event.
    """
    if repeated := _duplicates([c["name"] for c in checks]):
        raise SuiteImportInvalidError(
            "checks are matched by name, and the document names some more than once: "
            + ", ".join(repr(n) for n in repeated[:10]),
            detail={"duplicate_names": repeated[:20]},
        )
    existing = list(session.scalars(select(Check).where(Check.suite_id == suite.id)))
    wanted = {c["name"] for c in checks}
    if repeated := _duplicates([c.name for c in existing if c.name in wanted]):
        raise SuiteImportInvalidError(
            "checks are matched by name, and the suite has several checks named: "
            + ", ".join(repr(n) for n in repeated[:10])
            + " — rename them in the suite first",
            detail={"duplicate_names": repeated[:20]},
        )
    by_name = {c.name: c for c in existing}

    # (change, document check, resolved comparison source, the suite's check)
    planned: list[tuple[CheckChange, dict[str, Any] | None, uuid.UUID | None, Check | None]] = []
    for doc in checks:
        source_id = (

        current = by_name.get(doc["name"])
        if current is None:
            planned.append((CheckChange(doc["name"], "create", []), doc, source_id, None))
            continue
        if current.kind != doc["kind"]:
            raise SuiteImportInvalidError(
                f"check {doc['name']!r} is a {current.kind} check in the suite and a "
                f"{doc['kind']} check in the document; a check's kind cannot be changed — "
                "give the new check a different name",
                detail={"check_name": doc["name"]},
            )
        fields = _check_diff(current, doc, source_id)
        action = "update" if fields else "unchanged"
        planned.append((CheckChange(doc["name"], action, fields), doc, source_id, current))
    unmanaged = [c for c in existing if c.name not in wanted]
    if prune:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Scratch stack for the docs screenshot/video lane (frontend/e2e-docs/).
# Mirrors CI's frontend-e2e job — dev-bypass auth, seeded demo data — on its
# own database, OpenBao KV mount and ports, so the developer's compose stack
# (and its orphan-secret sweep) never sees it. Reuses the compose Postgres
# (:5432), Redis (:6379, db 3) and OpenBao (:8200).
#
#   scripts/docs/capture-stack.sh start    # migrate + seed + api :8001 + vite :3001
#   scripts/docs/capture-stack.sh capture  # run the e2e-docs Playwright project
#   scripts/docs/capture-stack.sh stop     # stop the processes (data kept)
#   scripts/docs/capture-stack.sh destroy  # stop + drop the database + the KV mount
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
RUN="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dataq-docs-capture"
mkdir -p "$RUN"
API_PORT="${DOCS_API_PORT:-8001}"
WEB_PORT="${DOCS_WEB_PORT:-3001}"
DB_NAME="${DOCS_DB_NAME:-dataq_docs}"
KV_MOUNT="${DOCS_KV_MOUNT:-docs-capture}"
COMPOSE=(docker compose -f "$ROOT/docker-compose.yml")
_env() {
  set -a
  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
  source "$ROOT/.env"
  set +a
  export DATABASE_URL="REDACTED"
  export REDIS_URL="redis://localhost:6379/3"
  export SECRET_STORE=openbao
  export OPENBAO_ADDR="http://localhost:8200"
  export OPENBAO_TOKEN
  export OPENBAO_MOUNT="$KV_MOUNT"
  export AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true
  # Explicitly NOT OTP: a developer's .env.app may configure it, and OTP wins
  # over dev-bypass at import time (core/auth.py).
  export AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_EMAILS= AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_DOMAINS= AUTH_EMAIL_SMTP_HOST= AUTH_EMAIL_FROM=
  export DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL=
  export ENVIRONMENT=dev
  export REDACTED@dataq.local
  export RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false

(cd "$ROOT" && nohup conda run -n dataq --no-capture-output \
      uvicorn backend.app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$API_PORT" >"$RUN/api.log" 2>&1 </dev/null & echo $! >"$RUN/api.pid")
  for _ in $(seq 1 40); do
    curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT}/api/v1/me" >/dev/null && break; sleep 1
  done
  curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT}/api/v1/me" >/dev/null || { echo "api did not come up"; tail -20 "$RUN/api.log"; exit 1; }
  # The seed carries no llm_settings row; the LLM captures need a saved, enabled
  # OpenAI-compatible config so a fresh stack regenerates the same images. The
  # key is a placeholder (Ollama ignores it); Test only shows OK when a server
  # answers at DOCS_LLM_BASE_URL.
  curl -sf -o /dev/null -X PUT -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    "http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT}/api/v1/admin/llm" \
    -d "{\"provider\":\"openai_compatible\",\"model\":\"${DOCS_LLM_MODEL:-qwen2.5:14b}\",\"base_url\":\"${DOCS_LLM_BASE_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1}\",\"api_key\":\"docs-capture-placeholder\",\"structured_output\":\"prompt_json\",\"enabled\":true}" \
    || { echo "could not seed the LLM provider config"; exit 1; }
  # Optional: a real Snowflake reader connection + suite, for the SQL-generation and
  # suggest-checks captures (both need to introspect a live table — a fake config
  # errors on every call). Skipped when DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT is unset, so the base
  # capture set still works with no warehouse credentials at hand; export it (plus
  # DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_USER/_SECRET, the rest default to the harness reader's shape —
  # DATAQ_DB.RETAIL, warehouse DATAQ_WH, role DATAQ_READER) before `start` to enable
  # them. `DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_SECRET` is read from the environment only — never logged,
  # never written to a file here.
  if [ -n "${DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT:-}" ]; then
    conn_id="$(curl -sf -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      "http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT}/api/v1/connections" \
      -d "{\"name\":\"snowflake-docs-reader\",\"type\":\"snowflake\",\"env\":\"dev\",\"config\":{\"account\":\"${DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT}\",\"user\":\"${DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_USER:?export DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_USER to enable the live-warehouse captures}\",\"database\":\"${DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE:-DATAQ_DB}\",\"schema\":\"${DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_SCHEMA:-RETAIL}\",\"warehouse\":\"${DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE:-DATAQ_WH}\",\"role\":\"${DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_ROLE:-DATAQ_READER}\",\"auth_type\":\"password\"},\"secret\":\"${DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_SECRET:?export DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_SECRET to enable the live-warehouse captures}\"}" \
      | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin).get("id",""))')" \
      || { echo "could not create the docs Snowflake connection"; exit 1; }
    if [ -z "$conn_id" ]; then
      echo "docs Snowflake connection created but the response carried no id — aborting rather than silently skipping the live-warehouse captures"; exit 1
    fi
    curl -sf -o /dev/null -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      "http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT}/api/v1/suites" \
      -d "{\"name\":\"Retail orders (reader)\",\"connection_id\":\"$conn_id\",\"target\":{\"table\":\"${DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_TABLE:-ORDERS_HEADER}\",\"schema\":\"${DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_SCHEMA:-RETAIL}\"}}" \
      || { echo "could not create the docs Snowflake suite"; exit 1; }
    echo "live-warehouse captures enabled (connection $conn_id)"
  fi
  (cd "$ROOT/frontend" && VITE_API_PROXY_TARGET="http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT}" VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true \
      nohup pnpm dev --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$WEB_PORT" --strictPort >"$RUN/web.log" 2>&1 </dev/null & echo $! >"$RUN/web.pid")

  # answers at DOCS_LLM_BASE_URL.
  curl -sf -o /dev/null -X PUT -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    "http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT}/api/v1/admin/llm" \
    -d "{\"provider\":\"openai_compatible\",\"model\":\"${DOCS_LLM_MODEL:-qwen2.5:14b}\",\"base_url\":\"${DOCS_LLM_BASE_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1}\",\"api_key\":\"docs-capture-placeholder\",\"structured_output\":\"prompt_json\",\"enabled\":true}" \
    || { echo "could not seed the LLM provider config"; exit 1; }
  # Optional: a real Snowflake reader connection + suite, for the SQL-generation and
  # suggest-checks captures (both need to introspect a live table — a fake config
  # errors on every call). Skipped when DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT is unset, so the base
  # capture set still works with no warehouse credentials at hand; export it (plus
  # DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_USER/_SECRET, the rest default to the harness reader's shape —
  # DATAQ_DB.RETAIL, warehouse DATAQ_WH, role DATAQ_READER) before `start` to enable
  # them. `DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_SECRET` is read from the environment only — never logged,
  # never written to a file here.
  if [ -n "${DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT:-}" ]; then
    conn_id="$(curl -sf -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      "http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT}/api/v1/connections" \
      -d "{\"name\":\"snowflake-docs-reader\",\"type\":\"snowflake\",\"env\":\"dev\",\"config\":{\"account\":\"${DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT}\",\"user\":\"${DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_USER:?export DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_USER to enable the live-warehouse captures}\",\"database\":\"${DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE:-DATAQ_DB}\",\"schema\":\"${DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_SCHEMA:-RETAIL}\",\"warehouse\":\"${DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE:-DATAQ_WH}\",\"role\":\"${DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_ROLE:-DATAQ_READER}\",\"auth_type\":\"password\"},\"secret\":\"${DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_SECRET:?export DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_SECRET to enable the live-warehouse captures}\"}" \
      | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin).get("id",""))')" \
      || { echo "could not create the docs Snowflake connection"; exit 1; }
    if [ -z "$conn_id" ]; then
      echo "docs Snowflake connection created but the response carried no id — aborting rather than silently skipping the live-warehouse captures"; exit 1
    fi
    curl -sf -o /dev/null -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      "http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT}/api/v1/suites" \
      -d "{\"name\":\"Retail orders (reader)\",\"connection_id\":\"$conn_id\",\"target\":{\"table\":\"${DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_TABLE:-ORDERS_HEADER}\",\"schema\":\"${DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_SCHEMA:-RETAIL}\"}}" \
      || { echo "could not create the docs Snowflake suite"; exit 1; }
    echo "live-warehouse captures enabled (connection $conn_id)"
  fi
  (cd "$ROOT/frontend" && VITE_API_PROXY_TARGET="http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT}" VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true \
      nohup pnpm dev --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$WEB_PORT" --strictPort >"$RUN/web.log" 2>&1 </dev/null & echo $! >"$RUN/web.pid")

content.content:
class CoverageFigures:
    """Workspace-wide (ADR 0037): the same for every member, and counts only — no asset,
    suite or incident is named.

    ``false_positive_rate`` is ``false_positive / stated``: of the automatic-suite
    incidents a person resolved AND classified in the window, the share marked
    false positive. Incidents resolved without a stated resolution (``unstated``) and
    auto-resolved ones are in neither number, so a low rate over few stated resolutions
    says little — read it with ``stated`` beside it.
    """

    assets_total: int
    assets_watched: int
    #: Watched by a suite a person authored (whether or not an automatic one watches too).
    assets_watched_authored: int
    #: Watched by automatic suites only.
    assets_watched_auto_only: int
    coverage_pct: float | None
    coverage_window_days: int
    false_positive_window_days: int
    #: Automatic-suite incidents a person resolved in the window.
    resolved: int
    stated: int
    unstated: int
    false_positive: int
    false_positive_rate: float | None


def coverage_figures(
    session: Session, *, false_positive_window_days: int = 30, now: datetime | None = None
) -> CoverageFigures:
    now = now or datetime.now(UTC)
    ran_since = now - timedelta(days=COVERAGE_WINDOW_DAYS)
    assets_total = session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Asset)) or 0
    # An asset is watched by an origin if a suite of that origin targeting it completed a
    # run in the window. `succeeded` only: a run that failed outright evaluated nothing.
    watched_rows = session.execute(
        select(Suite.asset_id, Suite.origin)
        .join(Run, Run.suite_id == Suite.id)
        .where(
            Suite.asset_id.is_not(None),
            Run.status.in_(AGGREGATABLE_RUN_STATUSES),
            Run.created_at >= ran_since,
        )
        .distinct()
    ).all()

class CoverageFigures:
    """Workspace-wide (ADR 0037): the same for every member, and counts only — no asset,
    suite or incident is named.

    ``false_positive_rate`` is ``false_positive / stated``: of the automatic-suite
    incidents a person resolved AND classified in the window, the share marked
    false positive. Incidents resolved without a stated resolution (``unstated``) and
    auto-resolved ones are in neither number, so a low rate over few stated resolutions
    says little — read it with ``stated`` beside it.
    """

    assets_total: int
    assets_watched: int
    #: Watched by a suite a person authored (whether or not an automatic one watches too).
    assets_watched_authored: int
    #: Watched by automatic suites only.
    assets_watched_auto_only: int
    coverage_pct: float | None
    coverage_window_days: int
    false_positive_window_days: int
    #: Automatic-suite incidents a person resolved in the window.
    resolved: int
    stated: int
    unstated: int
    false_positive: int
    false_positive_rate: float | None


def coverage_figures(
    session: Session, *, false_positive_window_days: int = 30, now: datetime | None = None
) -> CoverageFigures:
    now = now or datetime.now(UTC)
    ran_since = now - timedelta(days=COVERAGE_WINDOW_DAYS)
    assets_total = session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Asset)) or 0
    # An asset is watched by an origin if a suite of that origin targeting it completed a
    # run in the window. `succeeded` only: a run that failed outright evaluated nothing.
    watched_rows = session.execute(
        select(Suite.asset_id, Suite.origin)
        .join(Run, Run.suite_id == Suite.id)
        .where(
            Suite.asset_id.is_not(None),
            Run.status.in_(AGGREGATABLE_RUN_STATUSES),
            Run.created_at >= ran_since,
        )
        .distinct()
    ).all()
    origins: dict[uuid.UUID, set[str]] = {}
    for asset_id, origin in watched_rows:
        origins.setdefault(asset_id, set()).add(origin)
    authored = sum(1 for o in origins.values() if "user" in o)
    watched = len(origins)

    since = now - timedelta(days=false_positive_window_days)
    counts = dict(
        session.execute(
            select(Incident.resolution, func.count())
            .join(Suite, Suite.id == Incident.suite_id)
            .where(
                Suite.origin == "auto",
                Incident.status == "resolved",
                Incident.resolved_by == "user",
                Incident.resolved_at >= since,
            )
            .group_by(Incident.resolution)
        )
        .tuples()
        .all()
    )
    unstated = counts.pop(None, 0)
    stated = sum(counts.values())
    false_positive = counts.get("false_positive", 0)
    return CoverageFigures(
        assets_total=assets_total,
        assets_watched=watched,
        assets_watched_authored=authored,
        assets_watched_auto_only=watched - authored,
        coverage_pct=round(100.0 * watched / assets_total, 1) if assets_total else None,
        REDACTED,
        false_positive_window_days=false_positive_window_days,
        resolved=stated + unstated,
        stated=stated,
        unstated=unstated,
        false_positive=false_positive,
        false_positive_rate=round(100.0 * false_positive / stated, 1) if stated else None,
    )

"""Coverage of the inventory and the false-positive rate (ADR 0047 §8), on real Postgres."""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Any

import pytest

from backend.app.db.models import Asset, Check, Connection, Incident, Run, Suite, User
from backend.app.services import coverage_service as cov

NOW = datetime(2026, 10, 4, 12, 0, tzinfo=UTC)


@pytest.fixture
def conn(db_session: Any) -> Connection:
    owner = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email=f"{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@x.io")
    db_session.add(owner)
    db_session.flush()
    connection = Connection(
        name=f"pg-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}",
        type="postgres",
        env="dev",
        config={},
        secret_ref="kv",
        created_by=owner.id,
    )
    db_session.add(connection)
    db_session.commit()
    return connection


def _asset(db: Any, name: str) -> Asset:
    asset = Asset(namespace="postgres://h/db", name=name)
    db.add(asset)
    db.flush()
    return asset


def _suite(db: Any, conn: Connection, asset: Asset, *, origin: str) -> Suite:
    suite = Suite(
        name=f"s-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}",
        connection_id=conn.id,
        asset_id=asset.id,
        origin=origin,
        created_by=conn.created_by if origin == "user" else None,
    )
    db.add(suite)
    db.flush()
    return suite


def _run(db: Any, suite: Suite, *, days_ago: float, status: str = "succeeded") -> None:
    db.add(
        Run(
            suite_id=suite.id,
            status=status,
            triggered_by="manual",
            created_at=NOW - timedelta(days=days_ago),
        )
    )
    db.flush()


def _resolved(
    db: Any,
    suite: Suite,
    *,
    resolution: str | None,
    by: str = "user",
    days_ago: float = 1,
) -> None:
    check = Check(suite_id=suite.id, name=uuid.uuid4().hex[:8], expectation_type="e", config={})
    db.add(check)
    db.flush()
    db.add(
        Incident(
            asset_id=suite.asset_id,
            check_id=check.id,
            suite_id=suite.id,
            status="resolved",
            resolved_by=by,
            resolved_at=NOW - timedelta(days=days_ago),
            resolution=resolution,
        )
    )
    db.flush()


def test_coverage_counts_assets_with_a_recent_completed_run_and_splits_them(
    db_session: Any, conn: Connection
) -> None:
    authored, both, auto_only, stale, failed_only, unwatched = (
        _asset(db_session, n) for n in ("authored", "both", "auto", "stale", "failed", "none")
    )
    _run(db_session, _suite(db_session, conn, authored, origin="user"), days_ago=1)
    _run(db_session, _suite(db_session, conn, both, origin="user"), days_ago=2)
    _run(db_session, _suite(db_session, conn, both, origin="auto"), days_ago=2)
    _run(db_session, _suite(db_session, conn, auto_only, origin="auto"), days_ago=6)
    # Outside the 7-day window, and a run that never completed: neither watches anything.
    _run(db_session, _suite(db_session, conn, stale, origin="user"), days_ago=8)
    _run(
        db_session,
        _suite(db_session, conn, failed_only, origin="user"),
        days_ago=1,
        status="failed",
    )
    assert unwatched.id is not None

    figures = cov.coverage_figures(db_session, now=NOW)

    assert figures.assets_total == 6
    assert figures.assets_watched == 3
    assert (figures.assets_watched_authored, figures.assets_watched_auto_only) == (2, 1)
    assert figures.coverage_pct == 50.0
    assert figures.coverage_window_days == 7


def test_false_positive_rate_is_over_stated_resolutions_of_automatic_suites_only(
    db_session: Any, conn: Connection
) -> None:
    asset = _asset(db_session, "t")
    auto = _suite(db_session, conn, asset, origin="auto")
    authored = _suite(db_session, conn, asset, origin="user")
    _resolved(db_session, auto, resolution="false_positive")
    _resolved(db_session, auto, resolution="fixed")
    _resolved(db_session, auto, resolution="expected_change")
    _resolved(db_session, auto, resolution="fixed")
    _resolved(db_session, auto, resolution=None)  # resolved, did not say
    # None of these belong in the rate:
    _resolved(db_session, auto, resolution=None, by="auto")  # auto-resolved
    _resolved(db_session, auto, resolution="false_positive", days_ago=45)  # outside the window
    _resolved(db_session, authored, resolution="false_positive")  # a person's own suite
OPEN

- The false-positive rate of automatic checks is now split **by automatic check** (row count, freshness, column profile, schema, other checks in the automatic suite) and **by connection**, each as "false positives of stated" with its own rate. - Same data on three surfaces: the Dashboard's coverage panel, `GET /dashboard/coverage` and the MCP `get_coverage` tool (`false_positives_by_baseline`, `false_positives_by_connection`).

- Frontend: 3 new component tests; full suite 1747 passed.
- Not looked at in a browser with data: the seeded stack has no resolved incident on an automatic suite, so the tables render only in component tests.

## #1661 rules later work must respect (ADR 0047, amended 2026-10-13)

User decision 2026-10-13: automatic checks **inherit at run time**.
- Settings resolve asset override (`assets.auto_coverage_config`) → workspace (`coverage_settings` singleton) → built-in default. One resolver: `coverage_settings_service.resolve` / `for_suite` / `inherited_settings`.
- Sensitivity is per baseline (volume, freshness, profile); shape (window, min_points, seasonality) is shared. A level sets a group whole.
- The flag `inherit_coverage_settings` in check config is server-owned. REST/MCP reads never return it (they return effective values + `inherited` / `inherited_from`); export and `check_versions` do.
- Edit rule is `coverage_settings_service.settle_edit`: a sent value that differs from the one IN EFFECT pins the check; explicit `true` inherits and the numbers beside it are ignored; an omitted shape key on an inheriting check means unchanged.
- Stored threshold columns on an inheriting check are a creation-time snapshot, not what runs use. Any new reader of `checks.*_threshold` for an automatic anomaly check must go through the resolver.
- Recorded trade-off: shortening the window trims history; only the seasonality switch is lossless.

## Next, each waits on the user

**#1674 profiler PII classification source.** Five decisions in the issue comment of 2026-10-07
(identifier_column override, JSONB-on-assets vs a table, staleness, detector scope, lineage
propagation). User said 2026-10-13 they will pick it up after #1661.

**#1675 pii_drift kind.** Blocked on #1674. Needs its own migration PR first widening
`ck_checks_kind_valid` and `ck_monitor_baselines_kind_valid` (template `18f2ee7908cf`).

## Filed (open)

- #2413 (W6), #2416 (W6, P2), #2417 (W7) from the 2026-10-07 session.
- #2424 (W6, P3): `privacy_settings`, `scoring_settings`, `llm_settings` lack `CHECK (id = 1)` and their first save races (500). `coverage_settings_service.set_workspace` is the template fix.

## Environment facts

- Docker Desktop is NOT started by default (`open -a Docker`); it also restarted itself mid-suite once on 2026-10-13, which shows as mass `connection refused`, not test failures.
- `test_membership_service::test_removing_an_env_listed_row_names_the_variable_instead_of_404ing` fails locally on clean main (#2135). Not a regression.
- `frontend/.gitignore` ignores any directory named `coverage/`, including under `src/` and `tests/`: files there are silently never committed (hence `components/coverage-settings/`).
- `scripts/docs/capture-stack.sh start` hung after seeding on 2026-10-13; the API on :8001 was up, so starting Vite by hand (`VITE_API_PROXY_TARGET=http://127.0.0.1:8001 VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true pnpm dev --port 3001`) and running specs with `E2E_BASE_URL` worked. `destroy` cleans up. #1661 is closed: automatic checks now inherit their thresholds at run time, as you chose. It shipped as six PRs, all merged, and `main` is at `80841efeb` with zero open PRs. CI on `main` for the last merge was still running when I stopped.

| #2422 | ADR 0047 amendment |
| #2423 | Migration `543b75689c8c`: `coverage_settings` table and `assets.auto_coverage_config` |
| #2425 | Settings API: `/admin/coverage` and a per-table override |
| #2426 | Run-time inheritance in the run path, reconciler, check edits, REST and MCP reads |
| #2427 | UI: Admin → Settings → Automatic coverage, the asset page override, an "Inherited thresholds" tag |
| #2428 | False-positive rate split by automatic check and by connection |

## Design calls I made beyond your decision

- **Sensitivity is per baseline.** Row count, freshness and column profile each have their own warn / fail / critical. The history window is shared.
- **No per-connection level.** The ADR had promised per-connection tuning that was never built; it is now asset override → workspace setting → built-in default.
- **An edit detaches a check.** Changing a threshold or the window on an automatic check gives it its own values, and later setting changes no longer reach it. The editor says so, and offers a way back.
- **Shortening the window trims history.** The form warns before saving. Switching seasonality off and on loses nothing.

Say if you want any of these changed.

## What was not verified

- The "Inherited thresholds" tag, the editor notice and the false-positive tables were not seen in a browser with real data. The seeded stack has no automatic suite, so they are covered by component tests only.
- Nothing was run against a live warehouse. No SQL or driver handling changed.
- The first-save race fix on the settings row has no concurrent test.
- The full backend suite has one local failure, the known #2135.

## Other things to know

- I filed #2424: the three older settings tables (privacy, scoring, LLM) do not enforce one row, and their first save can race into a 500.
- Week 1 is at 3 of 5 and past its 2026-10-11 due date.
- The handover note in memory is updated.

#1674 is next. It needs your answers to the five decisions I listed earlier (identifier override, storage shape, staleness, detector scope, lineage propagation).

content.text:
Year-over-year seasonality doesn't fit the current baseline as built, so I need three decisions before designing it.

- **History:** an anomaly check keeps at most 8 weeks of observations (the window × 7), so there is nothing a year old to compare against.
- **Metric:** it can only watch whole-table row count, freshness and column profile. A sales table's row count only grows, so "this week vs the same week last year" on it says nothing about sale periods.
- **Cycle rule:** v1.3 is "no net-new features" by your own direction. This is one, so I'd file it as a new issue, with an ADR 0047 amendment if it touches automatic checks.

questions.question: What should be compared year over year?

options.label: Per-period value (Recommended)
options.description: A new metric bucketed by a date column: rows per day/week, or the sum of a column such as sales amount per day/week. This is what a sales team means by seasonality. Needs a date column chosen on the check.

options.label: Existing whole-table metrics
options.description: Keep row count, freshness and column profile, and only add a same-time-last-year comparison. Smaller, but on a growing sales table it will not reveal sale periods.

questions.question: Where does the year of history come from?

options.label: Backfill from the table (Recommended)
options.description: Compute past periods from the table's own date column in one query, so a check scores YoY on its first run. Only possible with the per-period metric, and it trusts that old rows are still in the table.

options.label: Accumulate from runs
options.description: Keep each run's observation for 2+ years. Works for any metric, but gives no YoY verdict for the first year and grows the stored baseline about 7x.

questions.question: What does 'identify the on-sale times of the year' mean for the product?

options.label: Detect and show them (Recommended)
options.description: DataQ finds the periods that recur as peaks across years and shows them as a seasonal calendar on the check's trend. A spike inside a known period is expected, not an alert; a missing peak is.

options.label: People declare them
options.description: An admin enters sale windows (e.g. late November, mid July). Checks treat those windows as expected. Simpler and exact, but nothing is discovered.

options.label: Both
options.description: Detect periods and let a person confirm, edit or add them. Most useful, largest scope.

options.label: Only the YoY baseline
options.description: No calendar. Just compare against the same period in earlier years, so a recurring sale stops raising false alarms.

class Observation:
    """One recorded measurement: when it was taken (UTC) and what it was."""

    ts: datetime
    value: float


# ───────────────────────── measurement ─────────────────────────


def measure_metric(
    connection: Connection,
    *,
    table: str,
    schema: str | None,
    catalog: str | None,
    params: AnomalyParams,
    secret_store: SecretStore,
    now: datetime,
) -> float:
    """This run's raw measurement of the configured ``target_metric``."""
    try:
        with _open_connection(connection, secret_store) as conn:
            dialect = conn.dialect if catalog is not None else None
            if params.target_metric == ROW_COUNT_METRIC:
                statement = build_monitor_statement(
                    VOLUME, table=table, schema=schema, catalog=catalog, config={}, dialect=dialect
                )
            else:
                statement = build_monitor_statement(
                    FRESHNESS,
                    table=table,
                    schema=schema,
                    catalog=catalog,
                    config={"column": params.column},
                    dialect=dialect,
                )
            scalar = conn.execute(statement).scalar()
    except ProfileUnsupportedError as exc:
        raise MonitorConfigError(
            f"anomaly monitors need a SQL datasource, not {connection.type!r}"
        ) from exc
    if params.target_metric == ROW_COUNT_METRIC:
        return float(row_count_from_scalar(scalar))
    source = f"MAX({params.column})"
    if scalar is None:
        # An empty table (or an all-NULL column) has no age.
        raise MonitorConfigError(f"{source} is unavailable, anomaly can't measure freshness age")
    return freshness_age_hours(scalar, now=now, source=source, column=params.column)


# ───────────────────────── column profile (ADR 0047) ─────────────────────────

NULL_PCT = "null_pct"
DISTINCT = "distinct"
_SERIES_SEP = "\x1f"
#: Spread floors, so a steady series is not flagged for a trivial change: null % never below
#: 1 percentage point, distinct count never below 10% of its mean.
_NULL_PCT_STDDEV_FLOOR = 1.0
_DISTINCT_STDDEV_FLOOR_RATIO = 0.1
#: Deviations named in the result, largest first.
_COLUMN_PROFILE_REPORTED = 10



def eligible_values(
    observations: list[Observation], *, now: datetime, params: AnomalyParams
) -> list[float]:
    """The prior values this run is scored against, newest-last."""
    considered = (
        [o for o in observations if o.ts.weekday() == now.weekday()]
        if params.seasonality
        else list(observations)
    )
    return [o.value for o in considered[-params.window :]]


def score(value: float, priors: list[float]) -> tuple[float, float, float, bool]:
    """``(z_score, mean, stddev, degenerate)`` for a value against its priors."""
    if len(priors) < 2:
        raise MonitorConfigError(
            f"anomaly scoring needs at least 2 prior points, got {len(priors)}"
        )
    mean = statistics.fmean(priors)
    stddev = statistics.stdev(priors)
    if stddev == 0.0:
        return (0.0 if value == mean else ANOMALY_DEGENERATE_Z), mean, stddev, True
    return abs(value - mean) / stddev, mean, stddev, False

    payload: dict[str, Any] = {
        "target_metric": params.target_metric,
        "value": value,
        "points": len(priors),
        "window": params.window,
        "min_points": params.min_points,
        "seasonality": params.seasonality,
    }
    if len(priors) < params.min_points:
        payload["insufficient_history"] = True
        payload["reason"] = "insufficient_history"
        return payload
    z_score, mean, stddev, degenerate = score(value, priors)
    payload.update(

            "mean": round(mean, 6),
            "stddev": round(stddev, 6),
            "deviation": round(value - mean, 6),
            "degenerate_stddev": degenerate,
        }
    )
    return payload

content.text:
Partly. The yearly baseline belongs in DataQ; finding sale periods for the CAGR team does not. Nothing is built or filed yet — I've only read code so far.

**Belongs in DataQ:**
- **Per-period metric:** rows or a column's sum per day or week, bucketed by a date column.
- **Yearly seasonality on that metric:** a recurring sale spike stops raising a false alarm, and a peak that should have arrived but didn't is flagged. That second case is a real data problem, such as a missing load.
- **Declared seasonal periods:** people state the sale windows so the check treats them as expected. I'd hold these once per workspace rather than per check, since a sale window is a business fact that applies across tables.

**Belongs elsewhere:**
- **Discovering when the sales are, as an answer for analysts.** That is business analysis, and the CAGR team's BI tool or notebook is the right place. DataQ can show the periods it detected on a check's trend chart as a by-product of the baseline, but I would not build it as a feature people come to DataQ for.

**Where inside DataQ:** the anomaly monitor as an authored check, not automatic coverage. Automatic checks assume nothing about a table, while this needs someone to pick the date column and the amount column. Automatic coverage could later suggest such a check for review.

One consequence of your "accumulate from runs" answer: there is no yearly verdict until a check has run for a year. Until then it scores on the ordinary rolling window.

So I'd narrow your "Both" answer: declared periods plus detected periods shown on the trend, both used only to judge the data, with no sale-period report. If that's right, I'll file the issue and write the ADR as the first PR. This is a net-new feature in a cycle you set as "no net-new features", so tell me if it should wait for v1.4 instead.

content.text:
Your instinct about the year is right, but it doesn't decide between the two options. Both use at least a year of data; they differ in where that year comes from.

- **Accumulate from runs:** DataQ starts with nothing and records one value per run. The first yearly comparison is possible after a year of waiting.
- **Backfill from the table:** on the first run, one query groups the table's existing rows by the date column. If the table already holds three years of sales, DataQ has three years of history on day one.

One year is also thin. With a single prior year DataQ cannot tell a recurring sale from a one-off spike; it needs two to call something recurring. With accumulation that means two years before the detected periods are trustworthy.

Accumulation does have real advantages:
- **It records what the data looked like at the time.** If history is later restated or late rows arrive, the baseline still reflects what each run actually saw.
- **It works when old rows are purged or archived.** Backfill has nothing to read there.
- **No large historical query.** Backfill is one scan of the whole table, which costs money on a per-query warehouse like Athena.

My recommendation is to do both: backfill once when the check is created to seed the history, then accumulate from every run after that. The seeded points would be marked as backfilled, so a result can say which kind of history it was scored against. If the table has less than a year of rows, the check simply waits, exactly as it would under your choice.

Do you want the seeded version, or accumulation only?

- **Status:** Accepted (2026-09-29)
- **Date:** 2026-09-29
- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771
- **Related:** ADR [0005](0005-severity-tier-weights.md) / [0016](0016-severity-derivation-semantics.md) (severity ladder), [0026](0026-auth-api-keys-and-principal-seam.md) (PATs), [0027](0027-suite-permission-model-workspace-admin.md) (per-suite `view`/`edit`), [0035](0035-request-rate-limiting.md) (rate limits); ADR [0004](0004-orchestration-abstraction.md) (the `OrchestrationProvider` contract this extends).

## Context

# ADR 0048 — Per-period metrics, yearly seasonality and seasonal periods on the anomaly monitor

- **Status:** Accepted (2026-10-13)
- **Date:** 2026-10-13
- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771
- **Related:** ADR [0012](0012-monitor-kind-seam.md) (monitor kinds, `metric_value`), [0016](0016-severity-derivation-semantics.md) (severity bands), [0041](0041-history-audit-strategy.md) (audit), [0047](0047-automated-coverage-loop.md) (automatic baselines, which this does not extend).

## Context

The anomaly monitor compares a run against the check's own recent history: the last few runs,
optionally the same weekday only. It watches three things, all of them whole-table: the row
count, the age of the newest timestamp, and the column profile. It keeps eight weeks of
observations at most.

That is the wrong shape for a table with a yearly rhythm. A sales table has sale periods. Its
whole-table row count only grows, so it says nothing about them. And if DataQ watched sales
per day instead, the last few weeks would be the wrong comparison twice over: every recurring
peak would look like an anomaly, and a peak that should have arrived and did not (a load that
failed during the sale) would look normal.

Two things are missing: a metric that is a value *per period*, and a baseline that knows what
this time of year usually looks like.

## Decision

1. **Two per-period metrics on the anomaly kind.** `period_row_count` counts the rows whose
   date falls in a period; `period_sum` sums a numeric column over them. The check names a
   `date_column`, a `period` (`day` or `week`) and, for the sum, a `value_column`. A run
   measures **complete** periods only, in UTC, with one pushdown aggregate over a half-open
   range of the date column. The verdict is about the last complete period.

   An observation is keyed by its period, not by when the run happened, so a second run in
   the same period replaces the value and does not add a point. Each run re-reads the trailing
   seven periods in the same query and updates them, because rows arrive late; only the last
   one is judged.

   These are authored checks on SQL datasources. They are **not** added to automatic coverage
   (ADR 0047): an automatic baseline assumes nothing about a table, and choosing which column
   is the business date and which is the amount is a claim a person makes.

2. **History is seeded once, then accumulated.** On the run that finds no baseline, one
   grouped query reads up to three years of complete periods from the table's own rows and
   stores them marked `backfilled`. Every later run adds what it measured, marked `observed`.
   The two are kept apart because they are different evidence: an observed point is what the
   table held when DataQ looked, and a backfilled point is what the table says today about
   the past, which a restatement or a purge can have changed. Each result reports how many of
   the points it was scored against were backfilled.

   Seeding is one scan of the table. It can be switched off on the check (`backfill: false`)
   for a warehouse that bills per query or a table whose old rows are archived; the check then
   starts empty and waits. Dropping a check's baseline seeds it again.

3. **Yearly seasonality is a seasonal index over the rolling baseline.** With `yearly: true`:

   - The *level* at a period is the median of the `window` periods before it.
   - The *index* for a period is what the same period in an earlier year was, divided by the
     level then. A day is matched to the same ISO week and weekday a year back; a week to the
     same ISO week. With more than one earlier year the index is their median.
   - The run's value and each prior value are divided by their index, and the ordinary
     z-score is taken over those. A sale that ran at 2.4 times its surrounding weeks last year
     is expected at 2.4 times now, so arriving at 2.4 times is normal and arriving flat is not.

   Every number in that chain is in the result: the level, the index, the years it came from,
   and the expected value. A period with no earlier year to match scores with an index of 1,
   which is exactly today's behaviour, and the result says the yearly comparison was not
   applied and why. Nothing is skipped for want of a year: the check is useful from the day it
   has `min_points`, and becomes seasonal when the history allows.

   Yearly seasonality is offered on the per-period metrics only. Weekday seasonality stays as
   it is and can be combined with it.

4. **Seasonal periods are declared by people and detected from history, and both are used
   only to judge the data.**

   - **Declared.** A workspace calendar of named periods, each either recurring (a month and
     day range, every year) or dated (explicit start and end, for a sale that moves). Admins
     manage it; changes are audited. It is workspace-wide because a sale period is a fact
     about the business, not about one check.
   - **Detected.** Read from a check's own history when asked: a run of periods at or above
     1.5 times the level. Seen at the same time in two or more years it is *recurring*; in one
     year, *seen once*. Detected periods are shown on the check's trend and can be promoted to
     the calendar by an admin. They are never stored as fact on their own.
   - **Effect.** Inside a declared period, a day is matched to the same offset within that
     period's previous occurrence, not to the same ISO week, which is what makes a moving
     sale line up. Periods inside a declared or recurring period are left out of the level, so
     the weeks after a sale are not judged against the sale. And a period inside a declared
     period with no earlier occurrence in the history is reported as `skip`, with that reason:
     DataQ has been told a peak is expected and has nothing to say how large.

5. **Retention.** A per-period check keeps three years of periods plus its window (about
   1,100 daily points), whatever its seasonality switches say. Other anomaly checks keep what
   they keep today.

## Phases

1. Per-period metrics: measurement, validation, observations keyed by period.
2. Seeding from the table and three-year retention.
3. Yearly seasonality in scoring.
4. The declared calendar (schema first, on its own).
5. Detected periods and the read surfaces (REST, MCP).
6. Check editor, trend view and calendar UI; user docs.

## Consequences

- A recurring peak stops paging people, and a missing one starts to.
- The first yearly verdict needs a year of history. Seeding supplies it where the table still
  holds its past; where it does not, the check waits a year, and says so on every result
  until then.
- One earlier year cannot tell a recurring sale from a one-off. The index uses it anyway,
  because one year is better than none, and the result names how many years stand behind it.
- A backfilled baseline trusts the table's history. Marking the points is what keeps that
  visible.
- Three years of daily points is a larger baseline row than any check has had. It is one JSONB
  value per check and is read once per run.

## Considered and rejected

- **A report of when the sales are**, for analysts to plan from: that is business analysis,
  and a BI tool is the place for it. DataQ shows the periods it detected because they explain
  its verdicts, not as a product of their own.
- **Accumulating only:** no yearly verdict for a year, and two before a period can be called
  recurring, on tables that already hold the history.
- **Backfilling only:** nothing would record what the table held when each run looked, so a
  later restatement would silently rewrite the baseline.
- **Year-over-year on the whole-table metrics:** a growing table's row count has no seasons.
- **Comparing only against the same period in earlier years:** two or three points give no
  spread to score against. The index keeps the recent window as the source of spread.
- **A forecasting library** (seasonal decomposition or similar): a new dependency whose
  verdict cannot be explained from the numbers in the result.
- **Declared periods on each check:** the same sale would be typed into every check that
  watches a table it touches.
- **Adding these checks to automatic coverage:** see decision 1. Automatic coverage may later
  *suggest* one for review.

content.text:
It's the other way round: the seasonality is designed for anomaly detection, and I had left automatic coverage out. I've now widened it to both, and the design is in [PR #2441](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/2441) (ADR 0048), which I've left open for you rather than merging. No code is written yet; the work is tracked in #2440.

## Where yearly seasonality applies

| Place | Yearly seasonality | History |
|---|---|---|
| Anomaly check on a per-period metric (rows or a sum per day/week) | Yes | Seeded from the table, then accumulated |
| Anomaly check on whole-table row count or freshness | Yes | Accumulated only; a past row count cannot be read back |
| Automatic row-count and freshness baselines | Yes, as a switch in the coverage settings, off by default | Accumulated only |
| Column profile (authored or automatic) | No | Hundreds of series per check, too large to keep for three years |
| Freshness, volume, aggregate and schema-drift monitors | No | They compare against fixed thresholds, so there is no baseline to make seasonal |

The anomaly monitor is the only place in DataQ with a learned baseline, so that is where it lives.

## Design calls in the ADR that need your yes

The review found seven problems in my first draft, and the fixes changed the design. These are my calls, not yours:

- **Scoring method:** this time last year is compared with its surrounding weeks, and that ratio sets what is expected now. With no earlier year the check behaves exactly as today and says so.
- **One stored point per period, written once.** Late-arriving rows do not revise a period already judged. A slow-filling table needs a longer settle delay (default 6 hours after the period closes).

"""Per-period anomaly metrics: rows or a sum per day or week, one point per period (ADR 0048)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from contextlib import contextmanager
from datetime import UTC, date, datetime
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import Any

import pytest
from sqlalchemy import text
from sqlalchemy.dialects import postgresql
from sqlalchemy.engine.default import DefaultDialect

from backend.app.datasources import monitors
from backend.app.datasources.monitors import MonitorConfigError, PeriodSpec, monitor_outcome
from backend.app.db.models import Check, Connection, Suite, User
from backend.app.services import anomaly
from backend.app.services.monitor_baseline import get_baseline
from backend.tests.support.fake_secret_store import FakeSecretStore

_COUNT = {"target_metric": "period_row_count", "date_column": "ordered_at"}
_SUM = {"target_metric": "period_sum", "date_column": "ordered_at", "value_column": "amount"}


def _spec(**overrides: Any) -> PeriodSpec:
    params = monitors.anomaly_params({**_COUNT, **overrides})
    assert params.period is not None
    return params.period


# ── config ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def test_defaults_are_a_utc_day_settled_for_six_hours() -> None:
    spec = _spec()

    assert (spec.unit, spec.timezone, spec.settle_hours, spec.value_column) == ("day", "UTC", 6, None)


def test_the_sum_metric_keeps_its_value_column_with_its_case() -> None:
    params = monitors.anomaly_params({**_SUM, "value_column": "NetAmount", "period": "week"})

    assert params.period == PeriodSpec("ordered_at", "week", "NetAmount", "UTC", 6)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "config",
    [
        {"target_metric": "period_row_count"},  # date_column is required
        {**_COUNT, "date_column": "a; DROP TABLE x"},
        {**_COUNT, "period": "month"},
        {**_COUNT, "period": None},
        {**_COUNT, "value_column": "amount"},  # a count sums nothing
        {"target_metric": "period_sum", "date_column": "ordered_at"},  # value_column required
        {**_SUM, "value_column": "a b"},
        {**_COUNT, "timezone": "Mars/Olympus"},
        {**_COUNT, "timezone": "../../etc/passwd"},
        {**_COUNT, "timezone": 5},
        {**_COUNT, "settle_hours": -1},
        {**_COUNT, "settle_hours": 169},
        {**_COUNT, "settle_hours": True},
        {**_COUNT, "column": "loaded_at"},  # the freshness key, not this metric's
    ],
)
def test_a_malformed_period_config_is_refused(config: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(MonitorConfigError):
        monitors.validate_monitor_config("anomaly", config)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("key", ["date_column", "period", "value_column", "timezone", "settle_hours"])
def test_a_period_key_on_a_whole_table_metric_is_refused_and_named(key: str) -> None:
    """Silently ignoring it would leave the author believing the check buckets by date."""
    with pytest.raises(MonitorConfigError, match=f"anomaly {key} applies only to"):
        monitors.anomaly_params({"target_metric": "row_count", key: "day"})


# ── which period is judged ───────────────────────────────────────────────────


def _at(iso: str) -> datetime:
    return datetime.fromisoformat(iso).replace(tzinfo=UTC)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("now", "overrides", "expected"),
    [
        # Tuesday 13 Oct 2026. Yesterday closed at 00:00 and settles at 06:00.
        ("2026-10-13T05:59", {}, (date(2026, 10, 11), date(2026, 10, 12))),
        ("2026-10-13T06:00", {}, (date(2026, 10, 12), date(2026, 10, 13))),
        ("2026-10-13T00:00", {"settle_hours": 0}, (date(2026, 10, 12), date(2026, 10, 13))),
        # 20:00 UTC is already 01:30 on the 14th in Kolkata, where the 13th has closed.
        (
            "2026-10-13T20:00",
            {"timezone": "Asia/Kolkata", "settle_hours": 1},
            (date(2026, 10, 13), date(2026, 10, 14)),
        ),
        ("2026-10-13T20:00", {"settle_hours": 1}, (date(2026, 10, 12), date(2026, 10, 13))),
        # Weeks run Monday to Sunday; the week of 5 Oct settled on Monday the 12th at 06:00.
        ("2026-10-12T05:59", {"period": "week"}, (date(2026, 9, 28), date(2026, 10, 5))),
        ("2026-10-12T06:00", {"period": "week"}, (date(2026, 10, 5), date(2026, 10, 12))),
        ("2026-10-18T23:00", {"period": "week"}, (date(2026, 10, 5), date(2026, 10, 12))),
    ],
)
def test_the_judged_period_is_the_last_one_closed_long_enough(
    now: str, overrides: dict[str, Any], expected: tuple[date, date]
) -> None:
    assert _spec(**overrides).settled(_at(now)) == expected


def test_a_daylight_saving_change_does_not_move_the_cut() -> None:
    """London fell back at 01:00 UTC on 25 Oct 2026. Six real hours after local midnight is
    05:00 UTC that day, not 06:00."""
    spec = _spec(timezone="Europe/London")

    assert spec.settled(_at("2026-10-26T05:59"))[1] == date(2026, 10, 25)
    assert spec.settled(_at("2026-10-26T06:00"))[1] == date(2026, 10, 26)
    # The day before the change, local midnight was 23:00 UTC, so it settles at 05:00 UTC.
    assert spec.settled(_at("2026-10-25T04:59"))[1] == date(2026, 10, 24)
    assert spec.settled(_at("2026-10-25T05:00"))[1] == date(2026, 10, 25)


# ── the statement ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def _compiled(config: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    params = monitors.anomaly_params(config)
    assert params.period is not None
    statement = monitors.period_statement(
        monitors.qualified_table(table="orders", schema="shop", catalog=None),
        params.period,
        start=date(2026, 10, 12),
        end=date(2026, 10, 13),
    )
    compiled = statement.compile(dialect=postgresql.dialect())
    return " ".join(str(compiled).split()), dict(compiled.params)


def test_the_count_statement_is_a_half_open_range_on_the_bare_column() -> None:
    sql, params = _compiled(_COUNT)

    assert sql == (
        "SELECT count(*) AS count_1 FROM shop.orders "
        "WHERE ordered_at >= %(period_start)s AND ordered_at < %(period_end)s"
    )
    assert params == {"period_start": date(2026, 10, 12), "period_end": date(2026, 10, 13)}


def test_the_sum_statement_quotes_mixed_case_columns() -> None:
    sql, _ = _compiled({**_SUM, "date_column": "OrderedAt", "value_column": "NetAmount"})

    assert 'sum("NetAmount")' in sql
    assert 'WHERE "OrderedAt" >=' in sql


def test_the_statement_gives_the_right_answer_on_a_real_database(db_session: Any) -> None:
    """Postgres only: what the query returns for a date column and for a timestamp column,
    with rows on both sides of each boundary."""
    db_session.execute(
        text(
            "CREATE TEMP TABLE period_orders (ordered_on date, ordered_at timestamp, "
            "amount numeric(10, 2)) ON COMMIT DROP"
        )
    )
    db_session.execute(
        text(
            "INSERT INTO period_orders VALUES "
            "('2026-10-11', '2026-10-11 23:59:59', 100), "
            "('2026-10-12', '2026-10-12 00:00:00', 10.50), "
            "('2026-10-12', '2026-10-12 23:59:59', 20.25), "
            "('2026-10-12', '2026-10-12 12:00:00', NULL), "
            "('2026-10-13', '2026-10-13 00:00:00', 1000)"
        )
    )
    target = monitors.qualified_table(table="period_orders", schema=None, catalog=None)

    def run(config: dict[str, Any], start: date, end: date) -> Any:
        spec = monitors.anomaly_params(config).period
        assert spec is not None
        return db_session.execute(
            monitors.period_statement(target, spec, start=start, end=end)
        ).scalar()

    day = (date(2026, 10, 12), date(2026, 10, 13))
    for column in ("ordered_on", "ordered_at"):
        count = {"target_metric": "period_row_count", "date_column": column}
        total = {"target_metric": "period_sum", "date_column": column, "value_column": "amount"}
        assert run(count, *day) == 3
        assert run(total, *day) == Decimal("30.75")
        assert run(count, date(2026, 10, 5), date(2026, 10, 12)) == 1
        # No row in the range: a count of 0, and SQL's NULL for the sum.
        assert run(count, date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 1, 2)) == 0
        assert run(total, date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 1, 2)) is None


# ── measuring ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def _connection() -> Connection:
    return Connection(
        id=uuid.uuid4(),
        name="pg",
        type="postgres",
        env="dev",
        config={"host": "h", "database": "shop", "user": "u"},
        secret_ref="ref",
        created_by=uuid.uuid4(),
    )


def _patch_scalar(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, scalar: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    seen: dict[str, Any] = {}

    class _Conn:
        dialect = DefaultDialect()

        def execute(self, statement: Any) -> Any:
            seen["statement"] = statement

            class _Res:
                @staticmethod
                def scalar() -> Any:
                    return scalar

            return _Res()

    @contextmanager
    def fake_open(connection: Connection, secret_store: Any) -> Any:
        yield _Conn()

    monkeypatch.setattr(anomaly, "_open_connection", fake_open)
    return seen


def _measure(config: dict[str, Any], now: str = "2026-10-13T12:00") -> float:
    return anomaly.measure_metric(
        _connection(),
        table="orders",
        schema="shop",
        catalog=None,
        params=monitors.anomaly_params(config),
        secret_store=FakeSecretStore(default="secret", raise_on_write=True),
        now=_at(now),
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("config", "scalar", "expected"),
    [
        (_COUNT, 412, 412.0),
        (_COUNT, Decimal("412"), 412.0),
        (_COUNT, "412", 412.0),  # a connector that hands COUNT back as text
        (_SUM, Decimal("30.75"), 30.75),
        (_SUM, 31, 31.0),
        (_SUM, 30.75, 30.75),
        (_SUM, None, 0.0),  # nothing in the period: zero was sold, not "unknown"
    ],
)
def test_measurement_accepts_what_drivers_return(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, config: dict[str, Any], scalar: Any, expected: float
) -> None:
    seen = _patch_scalar(monkeypatch, scalar)

    assert _measure(config) == expected
    assert dict(seen["statement"].compile().params) == {
        "period_start": date(2026, 10, 12),
        "period_end": date(2026, 10, 13),
    }


@pytest.mark.parametrize("scalar", ["30.75", True, float("nan"), b"30"])
def test_a_sum_that_is_not_a_finite_number_is_an_error_not_a_guess(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, scalar: Any
) -> None:
    _patch_scalar(monkeypatch, scalar)

content.content:
### Anomaly monitor (Snowflake / Unity Catalog / the generic SQL engines — ADR 0012)

*Is this value abnormal for this dataset?* Where a volume monitor asks "is the row
count inside a range I chose?", the anomaly monitor learns the range: it keeps a
rolling mean/stddev of the target's own **row count** or **freshness age** and bands
each run's **z-score** through the usual warn / fail / critical thresholds. Optional
**seasonality** makes the baseline weekday-aware, so a quiet Sunday isn't an anomaly
just for being smaller than Monday.

Below its `min_points` of history the check reports **skip**, never a fabricated
pass — a baseline that hasn't seen enough runs has no opinion. The per-check
**trend view** overlays the learned baseline band on the metric history so you can
see what "normal" currently means. SQL datasources only: the anomaly executor takes
its own measurement over a live SQL connection, which the natively-computed Iceberg
and flat-file monitor paths don't expose.

**Column profile** is a third target metric that watches every column at once. One
query per run measures each column's **null percentage** and **distinct count**, and
each of those gets its own history. The result names the columns that moved, largest
deviation first, and its metric (the z-score the thresholds read) is the largest one.

- A null rate is flagged whichever way it moves. A distinct count is flagged only when
  it **falls**: a growing table's distinct counts rise every day, but a column that
  collapses from 50 values to 1 is a problem.
- A column that has never had a null is not flagged for one stray null: the spread a
  null rate is measured against is never taken as less than 1 percentage point, and a
  distinct count's never as less than 10% of its mean.
- It measures the first 100 columns in table order and reports how many there are in
  total. A column whose type the engine can't cast to a string (Redshift `GEOMETRY` or `BOOLEAN`), or
  whose cast drops values (Redshift `SUPER` objects), keeps its null rate but gets no
  distinct count, and is listed under `distinct_unavailable`. Every other column is still
  counted.

For example, with `{"target_metric": "column_profile", "window": 8, "min_points": 3}` on
`orders`, three runs build the history. When a load then leaves `customer_email` empty,
the next run reports `customer_email` · `null_pct` · value `100` against a mean of about
`2`, and fails.

**Per-period metrics** watch a value for each calendar day or week instead of the whole
table: `period_row_count` is the rows whose date falls in the period, and `period_sum` is
the sum of a numeric column over them. Use them for a table that only grows, where the
whole-table row count has no "normal" to return to: orders per day, sales amount per week.

- `date_column` says which column dates a row, `period` is `day` or `week` (Monday to
  Sunday), and `period_sum` also names a `value_column`.
- Only **complete** periods are judged. `timezone` (an IANA name, default `UTC`) decides
  when a day ends, and a period is judged once it has been closed for `settle_hours`
  (default 6), so a suite that runs just after midnight does not judge yesterday before the
  nightly load has landed. Raise it for a table that fills in slowly.
- Each period gets **one** stored point, written the first time it is judged. Running the
  suite again the same day measures the period again and reports it, but the baseline keeps
  the first value, and rows that arrive later do not revise it. The result's `recorded` field
  says whether this run stored a point.
- A row is placed by the date the warehouse returns for `date_column`. A timestamp with a
  time zone is read in the warehouse session's zone, which DataQ does not set, so for such a
  column `timezone` only decides when a period counts as complete.
- A period with no rows counts as 0, for the sum as well.
- Changing `date_column`, `period`, `value_column` or `timezone` starts the history again,
  because the earlier points measured something else.

"amount", "window": 14, "min_points": 7}` on `orders`, run daily at 07:00 UTC, judges
yesterday's sales each morning against the fourteen days before it. The check editor does

  period of a date column, for tables whose whole-table row count only grows. A period is
  judged once it is complete and has settled (`timezone`, `settle_hours`), and each period

"""Run DataQ's own period_statement through the real Trino and MariaDB drivers."""
import os
from datetime import date

import sqlalchemy as sa

from backend.app.datasources import monitors
from backend.app.datasources.monitors import aggregate_value, row_count_from_scalar

    ("2026-10-11", "2026-10-11 23:59:59", "100.00"),
    ("2026-10-12", "2026-10-12 00:00:00", "10.50"),
    ("2026-10-12", "2026-10-12 23:59:59", "20.25"),
    ("2026-10-12", "2026-10-12 12:00:00", None),
    ("2026-10-13", "2026-10-13 00:00:00", "1000.00"),
]


def check(engine: sa.Engine, table: str, schema: str | None, catalog: str | None, setup: list[str]) -> None:
    with engine.connect() as conn:
        for statement in setup:
            conn.execute(sa.text(statement))
        target = monitors.qualified_table(table=table, schema=schema, catalog=catalog, dialect=conn.dialect if catalog else None)
        for column in ("ordered_on", "ordered_at"):

values = ", ".join(

        f"INSERT INTO memory.default.period_orders VALUES {values}",

)

"""A per-period check's history: seeded once from the table, then accumulated (ADR 0048)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from contextlib import contextmanager
from datetime import UTC, date, datetime
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import Any

import pytest
from sqlalchemy import text
from sqlalchemy.engine.default import DefaultDialect

from backend.app.datasources import monitors
from backend.app.datasources.monitors import MonitorConfigError
from backend.app.db.models import Check, Connection, Suite, User
from backend.app.services import anomaly, monitor_baseline
from backend.app.services.monitor_baseline import get_baseline
from backend.tests.support.fake_secret_store import FakeSecretStore

_COUNT = {"target_metric": "period_row_count", "date_column": "ordered_at"}
_SUM = {"target_metric": "period_sum", "date_column": "ordered_at", "value_column": "amount"}


def _at(iso: str) -> datetime:
    return datetime.fromisoformat(iso).replace(tzinfo=UTC)


# ── config and retention ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def test_seeding_is_on_unless_switched_off() -> None:
    on = monitors.anomaly_params(_COUNT).period
    off = monitors.anomaly_params({**_COUNT, "backfill": False}).period

    assert on is not None and off is not None
    assert (on.backfill, off.backfill) == (True, False)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", ["no", 0, 1, "false"])
def test_a_backfill_switch_that_is_not_a_boolean_is_refused(value: Any) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(MonitorConfigError, match="backfill must be true or false"):
        monitors.anomaly_params({**_COUNT, "backfill": value})


def test_the_backfill_switch_is_refused_on_a_whole_table_metric() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(MonitorConfigError, match="anomaly backfill applies only to"):
        monitors.validate_monitor_config(
            "anomaly", {"target_metric": "row_count", "backfill": False}
        )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("config", "kept"),
    [
        ({**_COUNT, "window": 14}, 14 + 3 * 366),
        ({**_COUNT, "window": 14, "seasonality": True}, 14 * 7 + 3 * 366),
        ({**_COUNT, "window": 8, "period": "week"}, 8 + 3 * 53),
        # Every other anomaly check keeps what it kept before.
        ({"target_metric": "row_count", "window": 14}, 14),
        ({"target_metric": "row_count", "window": 14, "seasonality": True}, 98),
    ],
)
def test_a_per_period_check_keeps_three_years_on_top_of_its_window(
    config: dict[str, Any], kept: int
) -> None:
    assert monitors.anomaly_params(config).retained_observations == kept


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("value", "expected"),
    [
        (date(2026, 10, 12), date(2026, 10, 12)),
        (datetime(2026, 10, 12, 0, 0), date(2026, 10, 12)),
        (datetime(2026, 10, 12, 0, 0, tzinfo=UTC), date(2026, 10, 12)),
        ("2026-10-12", date(2026, 10, 12)),
        ("2026-10-12 00:00:00", date(2026, 10, 12)),
    ],
)
def test_a_history_rows_day_accepts_what_drivers_return(value: Any, expected: date) -> None:
    assert monitors.history_day(value) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", [None, 20261012, "last tuesday", b"2026-10-12"])
def test_a_history_row_with_no_readable_day_is_an_error_that_names_only_its_type(
    value: Any,
) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(MonitorConfigError, match="is not a date") as exc_info:
        monitors.history_day(value)

    assert "tuesday" not in str(exc_info.value)


def test_the_history_statement_gives_one_row_per_day_on_a_real_database(
    db_session: Any,
) -> None:
    db_session.execute(
        text(
            "CREATE TEMP TABLE period_history (ordered_at timestamp, amount numeric(10, 2)) "
            "ON COMMIT DROP"
        )
    )
    db_session.execute(
        text(
            "INSERT INTO period_history VALUES "
            "('2026-10-08 23:59:59', 999), "  # before the range
            "('2026-10-09 00:00:00', 10.50), ('2026-10-09 18:00:00', 20.25), "
            "('2026-10-11 09:00:00', NULL), ('2026-10-11 10:00:00', 5), "
            "('2026-10-12 00:00:00', 999)"  # the end is exclusive
        )
    )
    target = monitors.qualified_table(table="period_history", schema=None, catalog=None)

    def rows(config: dict[str, Any]) -> list[tuple[Any, Any]]:
        spec = monitors.anomaly_params(config).period
        assert spec is not None
        statement = monitors.period_history_statement(
            target, spec, start=date(2026, 10, 9), end=date(2026, 10, 12)
        )
        return sorted(tuple(r) for r in db_session.execute(statement).all())

    assert rows(_COUNT) == [(date(2026, 10, 9), 2), (date(2026, 10, 11), 2)]
    assert rows(_SUM) == [
        (date(2026, 10, 9), Decimal("30.75")),
        (date(2026, 10, 11), Decimal("5.00")),
    ]


# ── seeding ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def _connection() -> Connection:
    return Connection(
        id=uuid.uuid4(),
        name="pg",
        type="postgres",
        env="dev",
        config={"host": "h", "database": "shop", "user": "u"},
        secret_ref="ref",
        created_by=uuid.uuid4(),
    )


class _Warehouse:
    """Stands in for the live connection: answers the history query with ``history`` and the
    period query with ``value``, and records which of the two it was asked."""

    def __init__(self, history: Any = (), value: Any = 100) -> None:
        self.history = history
        self.value = value
        self.asked: list[str] = []

    def install(self, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> _Warehouse:
        warehouse = self

        class _Res:
            def __init__(self, kind: str) -> None:
                self.kind = kind

            def scalar(self) -> Any:
                return warehouse.value

            def all(self) -> Any:
                if isinstance(warehouse.history, Exception):
                    raise warehouse.history
                return list(warehouse.history)

        class _Conn:
            dialect = DefaultDialect()

            def execute(self, statement: Any) -> Any:
                kind = "history" if "history_start" in statement.compile().params else "period"
                warehouse.asked.append(kind)
                return _Res(kind)

        @contextmanager
        def fake_open(connection: Connection, secret_store: Any) -> Any:
            yield _Conn()

        monkeypatch.setattr(anomaly, "_open_connection", fake_open)
        return self


def _seed(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, history: Any, config: dict[str, Any], before: date
) -> list[tuple[str, float, bool]]:
    _Warehouse(history).install(monkeypatch)
    points = anomaly.seed_history(
        _connection(),
        table="orders",
        schema="shop",
        catalog=None,
        params=monitors.anomaly_params(config),
        secret_store=FakeSecretStore(default="secret", raise_on_write=True),
        before=before,
    )
    return [(p.ts.date().isoformat(), p.value, p.observed) for p in points]


def test_seeding_starts_at_the_first_day_with_rows_and_counts_later_gaps_as_zero(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    history = [(date(2026, 10, 8), 40), (date(2026, 10, 9), Decimal("55")), ("2026-10-11", "30")]

    points = _seed(monkeypatch, history, _COUNT, date(2026, 10, 13))

    # Nothing before the 8th is invented; the 10th and the 12th had no rows, so zero.
    assert points == [
        ("2026-10-08", 40.0, False),
        ("2026-10-09", 55.0, False),
        ("2026-10-10", 0.0, False),
        ("2026-10-11", 30.0, False),
        ("2026-10-12", 0.0, False),
    ]


def test_seeding_adds_days_up_into_weeks(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    history = [
        (date(2026, 9, 28), Decimal("10.50")),  # Monday
        (date(2026, 10, 4), Decimal("1.25")),  # Sunday of the same week
        (date(2026, 10, 5), None),  # a day whose amounts were all NULL
        (date(2026, 10, 7), Decimal("4")),
    ]

    points = _seed(monkeypatch, history, {**_SUM, "period": "week"}, date(2026, 10, 12))

    assert points == [("2026-09-28", 11.75, False), ("2026-10-05", 4.0, False)]


def test_seeding_a_table_with_no_rows_in_range_gives_no_history(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    assert _seed(monkeypatch, [], _COUNT, date(2026, 10, 13)) == []


def test_seeding_ignores_a_row_dated_outside_the_range_it_asked_for(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """A warehouse session in another zone can cast a boundary row to the day outside."""
    history = [(date(2026, 10, 13), 999), (date(2026, 10, 12), 7)]

    assert _seed(monkeypatch, history, _COUNT, date(2026, 10, 13)) == [("2026-10-12", 7.0, False)]


def test_seeding_reads_back_no_further_than_the_years_kept(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    warehouse = _Warehouse([]).install(monkeypatch)
    seen: dict[str, Any] = {}
    real = monitors.period_history_statement

    def spy(target: Any, spec: Any, *, start: date, end: date) -> Any:
        seen.update(start=start, end=end)
        return real(target, spec, start=start, end=end)

    monkeypatch.setattr(anomaly, "period_history_statement", spy)
    anomaly.seed_history(
        _connection(),
        table="orders",
        schema="shop",
        catalog=None,
        params=monitors.anomaly_params(_COUNT),
        secret_store=FakeSecretStore(default="secret", raise_on_write=True),
        before=date(2026, 10, 13),
    )

    assert seen == {"start": date(2023, 10, 12), "end": date(2026, 10, 13)}
    assert warehouse.asked == ["history"]


# ── the executor ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


@pytest.fixture
def graph(db_session: Any) -> tuple[Any, Connection, Check]:
    user = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email=f"u-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@x.io")
    db_session.add(user)
    db_session.flush()
    conn = _connection()
    conn.created_by = user.id
    db_session.add(conn)
    db_session.flush()
    suite = Suite(
        name=f"s-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
        connection_id=conn.id,
        created_by=user.id,
        target={"schema": "shop", "table": "orders"},
    )
    db_session.add(suite)
    db_session.flush()
    check = Check(
        suite_id=suite.id,
        name="daily orders",
        kind="anomaly",
        expectation_type="monitor:anomaly",
        config={**_COUNT, "window": 5, "min_points": 3},
        fail_threshold=Decimal("3"),
    )
    db_session.add(check)
    db_session.flush()
    return db_session, conn, check


_HISTORY = [(date(2026, 10, day), 100 + day) for day in range(5, 12)]  # the 5th to the 11th


def _run(
    graph: tuple[Any, Connection, Check], now: str, *, persist: bool = True
) -> Any:
    session, conn, check = graph
    outcome = anomaly.build_anomaly_executor(
        session,
        connection=conn,
        target_table="orders",
        target_schema="shop",
        target_catalog=None,
        secret_store=FakeSecretStore(default="secret", raise_on_write=True),
        persist=persist,
        clock=lambda: _at(now),
    )(check)
    session.flush()
    return outcome


def _stored(graph: tuple[Any, Connection, Check]) -> list[tuple[str, float, str]]:
    session, _, check = graph
    row = get_baseline(session, check.id)
    assert row is not None
    return [
        (o["ts"][:10], o["value"], o.get("source", "observed"))
        for o in row.baseline["observations"]
    ]


def test_the_first_run_seeds_the_past_and_scores_at_once(
    graph: tuple[Any, Connection, Check], monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    warehouse = _Warehouse(_HISTORY, value=108).install(monkeypatch)

    outcome = _run(graph, "2026-10-13T12:00")

    stored = _stored(graph)
    assert warehouse.asked == ["period", "history"]
    # Everything before the judged day is what the table says today; the judged day is what
    # this run saw.
    assert [s for _, _, s in stored] == ["backfilled"] * 7 + ["observed"]
    assert stored[0] == ("2026-10-05", 105.0, "backfilled")
    assert stored[-1] == ("2026-10-12", 108.0, "observed")
    assert outcome.observed_value["seeded"] == {"status": "done", "points": 7, "from": "2026-10-05"}
    # Scored on its first run, against the last five seeded days.
    assert outcome.skipped is False
    assert outcome.observed_value["history"] == {"backfilled": 5, "observed": 0}


def test_a_later_run_does_not_seed_again_and_the_marks_never_change(
    graph: tuple[Any, Connection, Check], monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    warehouse = _Warehouse(_HISTORY, value=108).install(monkeypatch)
    _run(graph, "2026-10-13T12:00")
    warehouse.asked.clear()

    outcome = _run(graph, "2026-10-14T12:00")

    assert warehouse.asked == ["period"]
    assert "seeded" not in outcome.observed_value
    assert outcome.observed_value["history"] == {"backfilled": 4, "observed": 1}
    assert [s for _, _, s in _stored(graph)] == ["backfilled"] * 7 + ["observed"] * 2


def test_with_seeding_off_the_check_starts_empty_and_asks_for_no_history(
    graph: tuple[Any, Connection, Check], monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    session, _, check = graph
    check.config = {**check.config, "backfill": False}
    session.flush()
    warehouse = _Warehouse(_HISTORY, value=108).install(monkeypatch)

    outcome = _run(graph, "2026-10-13T12:00")

    assert warehouse.asked == ["period"]
    assert outcome.observed_value["seeded"] == {"status": "off"}
    assert outcome.skipped is True
    assert _stored(graph) == [("2026-10-12", 108.0, "observed")]


def test_a_seeding_query_that_fails_does_not_fail_the_check(
    graph: tuple[Any, Connection, Check], monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    _Warehouse(RuntimeError("relation shop.orders: permission denied"), value=108).install(
        monkeypatch
    )

    outcome = _run(graph, "2026-10-13T12:00")

    assert outcome.errored is False and outcome.skipped is True
    assert outcome.observed_value["seeded"]["status"] == "failed"
    # The driver's message is not the reason shown.
    assert "permission denied" not in str(outcome.observed_value["seeded"])
    assert _stored(graph) == [("2026-10-12", 108.0, "observed")]


def test_a_dry_run_never_seeds(
    graph: tuple[Any, Connection, Check], monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    warehouse = _Warehouse(_HISTORY, value=108).install(monkeypatch)

    outcome = _run(graph, "2026-10-13T12:00", persist=False)

    session, _, check = graph
    assert warehouse.asked == ["period"]
    assert "seeded" not in outcome.observed_value
    assert get_baseline(session, check.id) is None


def test_dropping_the_baseline_seeds_it_again(
    graph: tuple[Any, Connection, Check], monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    session, _, check = graph
    warehouse = _Warehouse(_HISTORY, value=108).install(monkeypatch)
    _run(graph, "2026-10-13T12:00")
    _run(graph, "2026-10-14T12:00")

    monitor_baseline.rebaseline(session, check)
    session.flush()
    warehouse.asked.clear()
    outcome = _run(graph, "2026-10-15T12:00")

    assert warehouse.asked == ["period", "history"]
    assert outcome.observed_value["seeded"]["status"] == "done"
    assert _stored(graph)[-1] == ("2026-10-14", 108.0, "observed")


def test_changing_what_the_check_buckets_by_seeds_the_new_history(
    graph: tuple[Any, Connection, Check], monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    session, _, check = graph
    warehouse = _Warehouse(_HISTORY, value=108).install(monkeypatch)
    _run(graph, "2026-10-13T12:00")

    check.config = {**check.config, "date_column": "shipped_at"}
    session.flush()
    warehouse.history = [(date(2026, 10, 10), 7), (date(2026, 10, 11), 9)]
    warehouse.asked.clear()
    _run(graph, "2026-10-13T18:00")

    assert warehouse.asked == ["period", "history"]
    assert _stored(graph) == [
        ("2026-10-10", 7.0, "backfilled"),
        ("2026-10-11", 9.0, "backfilled"),
        ("2026-10-12", 108.0, "observed"),
    ]


def test_three_years_of_seeded_days_survive_the_trim(
    graph: tuple[Any, Connection, Check], monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    from datetime import timedelta

    start = date(2023, 10, 12)
    history = [(start + timedelta(days=i), 100) for i in range((date(2026, 10, 12) - start).days)]
    _Warehouse(history, value=100).install(monkeypatch)

    _run(graph, "2026-10-13T12:00")

    stored = _stored(graph)
    assert (stored[0][0], stored[-1][0], len(stored)) == ("2023-10-12", "2026-10-12", 1097)

    first run instead of waiting ``min_points`` runs. Those points are what the
    table says *today* about the past, not what it held then: a restatement or a
    purge since will have changed them. ``observed_value.history`` on every
    result gives how many of the points it was scored against were
    ``backfilled`` and how many a run ``observed``; say so when most are
    backfilled. ``observed_value.seeded`` on the seeding run reports ``status``
    (``done`` with the point count, ``off`` when ``backfill`` is false, or
    ``failed``: the check ran but started with no history). A ``done`` with
    ``points: 0`` means the table had no rows before the judged period, not that
    seeding was skipped. It is one full scan of the table; pass
    ``backfill=false`` in the config for a warehouse billed per query.
''' + s[j:]
p.write_text(s)
EOF
